text:
Quinton Byfield looks like a player taking the next step, and the scoresheet hasn't noticed yet. The Kings have him on the ice for 81% of their power-play chances, up from 44% last season, he's averaging 19.4 minutes, and his own chance quality has climbed to 1.27 expected goals per 60 from 0.82 (expected goals measure how good the chances were).

The return so far: 5 goals on 7.4 expected and 7 points in 18 games, a lower rate than last season. With him on the ice the Kings have scored 9.3 fewer goals than their chances deserved, and at five on five they take about 55% of the expected goals, more than five points better than when he sits. That is the profile of a player who's due, not one who's fading.

Evolving-Hockey had him at the 90th percentile among forwards for driving play last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 62% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Eighteen games is a small sample. We'd watch the power play: that's where the points should show up first.
headline: Byfield's breakout is hiding behind bad luck
